notes.statement: Ji et al. (2016) found that mice with B cell-specific deletion of Sel1l (Sel1L-CD19) looked healthy and grew normally. However, they had smaller spleens and 60 to 75% fewer peripheral B cells in spleen, blood, and lymph nodes, while T cells and myeloid cells were unaffected. B cell development was severely blocked at the transition from large to small pre-B cells.
quotes: The percentage of peripheral B cells in spleen, blood, and lymph nodes was reduced by 60-75% (Fig. 1E) and the absolute numbers of splenic B cells were >75% lower in Sel1LCD19 mice compared to controls
Thus, B cell-specific Sel1L deficiency results in a severe developmental defect at the transition from the large to small pre-B cells.

notes.statement: Ji et al. (2016) found that the developmental block in Sel1L-CD19 mice did not depend on Chop and was not explained by increased cell death. Large pre-B cells kept proliferating, with more than 2.5-fold more proliferation of lambda-5-positive large pre-B cells.
quotes: Thus, B cell-specific Sel1L deficiency results in a developmental block in a Chop-independent manner.
Among them, only λ5+ large pre-B cells were highly proliferative in Sel1LCD19 mice, increasing more than 2.5 fold; whereas λ5− pro-B cell proliferation did not increase in Sel1LCD19 mice.

notes.statement: Ji et al. (2016) showed that the Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD complex recognizes the pre-B cell receptor (pre-BCR) complex and targets it for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation in a BiP-dependent manner. Without Sel1L, the pre-BCR built up inside the cell and at the cell surface, and pre-BCR signaling persisted. Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD did not degrade the mature BCR.
quotes: Thus, we concluded that Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD recognizes and targets the pre-BCR complex for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and that Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD deficiency leads to intracellular accumulation of the pre-BCR.
Therefore, we concluded that the pre-BCR, but not the BCR, complex is an endogenous Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD substrate.
Hence, we concluded that BiP, but not the unique region of λ5, is required for the recognition of the pre-BCR complex as an ERAD substrate in pre-B cells.

notes.statement: Ji et al. (2016) found that loss of Sel1L or Hrd1 in 70z/3 pre-B cells raised the levels of all 3 pre-BCR components and stabilized Ig-mu heavy chain, extending its half-life from about 60 minutes to more than 120 minutes. It also increased phosphorylation of Syk, a kinase downstream of the pre-BCR.
quotes: Loss of either Sel1L or Hrd1 in the 70z/3 cells increased steady-state protein levels of all three components of the pre-BCR complex (Fig. 4B-C), and led to Igμ protein stabilization, with its half-life increasing from approximately 60 min to over 120 min (Fig. 4D).
Phosphorylation of the pre-BCR key downstream effector, spleen tyrosine kinase (Syk), was significantly increased in ERAD-deficient pre-B cells (Fig. 5G)
